_comment: Thresholds set from measurement, not from aspiration -- but be clear
about which machine each number came from.
Four runs against one unchanged build on the DEV VPS, which is loaded,
accessibility, best-practices and SEO returned 100 every time. The first
run on the CI RUNNER, which is what actually enforces this file, scored
100 across all four with 0ms blocking time.
So runner variance is not yet characterised -- one sample is not a range.
The floors stay where they are until it is. The three stable categories
are held near where they are, because a drop there is a real regression a
human introduced. The performance floor is deliberately loose: it catches
a catastrophe (a render-blocking script, an unoptimised hero image) and is
NOT a target. Passing it is not evidence of anything.
Raising the performance floor toward the observed 100 needs several runner
samples first. A guard that fails at random gets ignored, which costs more
Read the reported numbers in the job summary for the real signal.
